segments.t: Backstage at the ASK thirtieth anniversary gala, Camille alerts Hicham that the packed room is waiting for him. Noticing his nervous tension, she brings him a glass of water before he steps up to the microphone. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Hicham, tout le monde vous attend là-bas.
La salle entière est déjà bien remplie?
Oui, tous les artistes célèbres sont arrivés.
J'avoue que j'ai un trac terrible.
Ça va être à vous de monter.
J'ai préparé quelques mots très simples.
Je vais vous chercher un verre d'eau.
Merci Camille, vous êtes toujours très prévenante.
Pardonnez-moi, je me faufile rapidement.
Cette trentième fête d'anniversaire est grandiose.
Votre discours va énormément toucher l'assemblée.

Let's break down the dialogue line by line.
Hicham, tout le monde vous attend là-bas.
'Hicham, everyone is waiting for you over there.' Camille points across the crowded room. The present tense verb indicates the expectant crowd.
La salle entière est déjà bien remplie?
'Is the entire hall already well filled?' Hicham asks about the audience. The descriptive adjective phrase gauges the pressure on stage.
Oui, tous les artistes célèbres sont arrivés.
'Yes, all the famous artists have arrived.' Camille confirms the glamorous turnout. The compound past verb highlights the distinguished guests.
J'avoue que j'ai un trac terrible.
'I confess that I have terrible stage fright.' Hicham reveals his underlying anxiety. The noun phrase vividly describes public speaking jitters.
Ça va être à vous de monter.
'It is going to be your turn to go up.' Camille gives the official countdown. The near-future verbal idiom signals his upcoming turn at the microphone.
J'ai préparé quelques mots très simples.
'I prepared a few very simple words.' Hicham clutches his prompt cards. The compound past verb stresses his desire for heartfelt brevity.
Je vais vous chercher un verre d'eau.
'I will get you a glass of water.' Camille steps away to fetch a drink. The near-future construction promises immediate assistance.
Merci Camille, vous êtes toujours très prévenante.
'Thank you Camille, you are always very thoughtful.' Hicham expresses sincere gratitude. The complimentary adjective praises her professional attentiveness.
Pardonnez-moi, je me faufile rapidement.
'Pardon me, I am slipping through quickly.' Camille squeezes past the VIPs. The polite imperative verb excuses her brisk movement in the crowd.
Cette trentième fête d'anniversaire est grandiose.
'This thirtieth anniversary party is grandiose.' Hicham takes in the lavish hall. The ordinal numeral celebrates thirty years of cinematic history.
Votre discours va énormément toucher l'assemblée.
'Your speech will touch the audience enormously.' Camille offers encouraging support. The near-future verb with an adverb boosts his confidence.
Je veux surtout rendre hommage aux agents.
'I especially want to pay tribute to agents.' Hicham defines his noble purpose. The idiomatic verbal phrase underscores collective corporate honor.
Buvez cette eau fraîche avant de commencer.
'Drink this fresh water before starting.' Camille delivers the soothing glass. The imperative verb urges him to clear his throat.
Je suis maintenant prêt pour la scène.

'I am now ready for the stage.' Hicham takes a deep breath and steps forward. The predicate adjective announces his complete readiness. Now listen to the scene again at normal speed and see how much you understand.
